intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array ahead of the axle with moderate track, wheel and mass values. It gives the Integrator a balanced platform to tune and tests whether 15 mm sensor spacing with 12 mm footprints resolves the line well enough through the bends. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend at moderate speed, with line-loss events and rms error as the main weak points.
learning: Hypotheses to test: (1) 15 mm sensor spacing with 12 mm footprints is fine enough that the centre-line error signal stays linear within about ±20 mm. (2) Sensors placed 50 mm ahead of the axle give enough lead to avoid oscillation at moderate speed. (3) A 0.8 kg robot with 0.12 m track can turn fast enough for the slalom without line loss. Next measurements to request: per-track rms_error and max_error to locate where the error grows, and line_loss_events to see whether the sensor span is wide enough on the sharpest bends.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. The geometry is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Five sensors at 15 mm spacing, from x = -0.03 to +0.03, cover a 0.06 m band, which is about 2.4 times the 25 mm tape width. That keeps the line visible through moderate lateral error, and the centre sensor gives a clean reading near the centre line. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the robot sees the line before the wheels reach it, which leaves room for steering lag. Sensor size is 0.012 m, close to the tape width, so each footprint is mostly on or off the tape and the readings stay sharp. Wheel track is 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m, mid-range values that give moderate turn authority without excessive yaw sensitivity. Body width is 0.12 m, which sets the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. That is a safe margin against the 25 mm tape. Mass is 0.8 m, which keeps inertia moderate for quick speed changes. The expected result is a first completion on the oval, with the main failure modes (line loss on tight bends, overshoot) exposed for the Integrator to measure.
